title: Copy a file
description:
Copy one file to another with `open`, `read`, `write` and `close`.

```
wrote in.txt (18 bytes)
copied 18 bytes to out.txt
missing.txt: open failed (error 2)
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

SYS_READ equ    0
SYS_WRITE equ   1
SYS_OPEN equ    2
SYS_CLOSE equ   3

        section .data
in_name: db     "in.txt", 0
text:   db      "some text to copy", 10
text_len equ    $ - text

        section .bss
buf:    resb    64

        section .text
_start:
        ; TODO

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: `O_WRONLY` is 1, `O_CREAT` is 0x40 and `O_TRUNC` is 0x200 on Linux x86-64; the mode `0644` is `0o644` in NASM (lesson 7.03).
Keep the two file descriptors in `rbx` and `r12`; `test rax, rax` / `js .error` after each call.
requirements: Create `in.txt` first with `open` (flags `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC`, mode `0644`).
Copy in a loop of `read` into a 64-byte buffer and `write` of what was read, until `read` returns 0.
A negative return value from a system call is `-errno`; print the error number and close what is open.
stretch: Take the file names from the command line (`[rsp + 16]` and `[rsp + 24]` at `_start`).
